name: Voter Registration Data Breach
description: An intrusion exposes the voter registration database — names, addresses, birthdates, and partial IDs — weeks before a general election.
effect: Voter data exposure and confidence damage
assumptions: Much of the roll is public record; the breach story, not the data, drives confidence damage.
Primary loss covers forensics, notification, and state/federal coordination.
Secondary loss covers public-communication campaigns and litigation over roll integrity.

name: Results Website Defacement
description: Attackers deface the unofficial results page or seed manipulated numbers on election night, fueling disinformation even though official tallies are unaffected.
assumptions: Official canvass results are on separate systems; the harm is public perception.
Primary loss covers restoration, forensics, and emergency communications.
Secondary loss covers sustained public-trust remediation and legislative inquiries.

name: Ransomware Near an Election
description: Ransomware hits election-office systems in the pre-election window, disrupting pollbook preparation, mail-ballot processing, and staff scheduling.
threat: Ransomware affiliate indifferent to election timing
assumptions: Voting equipment is air-gapped; the loss is administrative recovery under deadline pressure.
State and federal partners provide surge support, reflected in the estimates.
Secondary loss covers emergency procedures litigation and confidence repair.

name: Election Night DDoS
description: DDoS attacks hit results reporting and the county site on election night, exactly when public and media attention peaks.
asset: Results reporting availability on election night
threat: DDoS operators timed to the election
effect: Results reporting outage at peak attention
assumptions: Attacks cluster on a handful of predictable nights per cycle.
Primary loss covers mitigation and manual media briefings during the outage.
Secondary loss reflects disinformation traction while official numbers are unreachable.

name: Spear Phishing of Election Officials
description: Targeted phishing against election staff seeks credentials for election-adjacent systems, echoing documented campaigns against county officials.
asset: Election staff accounts and adjacent systems
assumptions: Campaigns intensify in election years; staff emails are public records.
Primary loss covers response, resets, and mandatory incident reporting.
Secondary loss covers federal notification duties and public-disclosure fallout.
